text: Confine the Wasm runtime (Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception for Wasmtime) to userspace and forbid in-kernel Wasm execution on license grounds.
rationale: The runtime's license is GPLv2-incompatible so any kernel-side embedding is blocked regardless of technical merit.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Decide whether Wasm components and native components share one IDL and one interface registry or maintain a mapping layer between WIT and the native IDL.
rationale: A shared IDL fulfils the 'participate naturally' goal but constrains the native IDL to WIT's evolution.

lens: Research spikes and decisions that must precede commitments
text: Evaluate Wasm runtimes (Wasmtime, WAMR, others) for instantiation latency, memory footprint and capability binding, and decide the system runtime.
rationale: Wasm plugins must be cheap enough to be the default extension mechanism or they will be bypassed by native code.

text: Study the WebAssembly Component Model and WASI as architectural inputs to the native component and interface model; document adopted and rejected ideas.
Do not duplicate concepts that already have strong ecosystem momentum (e.g. WIT, WASI interfaces) without justification.
Support both native machine-code components and portable WebAssembly components as component kinds.
Wasm is a first-class format for plugins.
Wasm is a first-class format for sandboxed extensions.
Wasm is a first-class format for portable services.
Wasm is a first-class format for automation modules (see §45).
Wasm is a first-class format for downloaded components.
Wasm is a first-class format for cross-architecture workloads.
The native component model must map cleanly enough that Wasm components participate in the same object/capability/interface ecosystem (capabilities as WASI resources, channels as WIT interfaces).
ADR: choose the Wasm runtime (wasmtime, wasmer, custom) and whether it runs in-component or as a shared service.
Do not force every application into WebAssembly; native machine code remains a first-class target.
Study the WebAssembly Component Model (WIT, resources, interface versioning) as a candidate IDL/type-system foundation.
Study WASI capability-based system interfaces for alignment between Wasm components and native capabilities.
